Step 2 · Test your voice

First, test your voice

  1. aIt asks what to call it. Don't answer yet. Tap the mic at the bottom
  2. biPhone asks: tap Allow
  3. cThe timer counts up. Say a few words and check they show up
Before you answer, tap the mic and make sure voice works. You'll talk to your bot a lot.
Then answer the name quickly. Any name works for now. You'll give it its real name and job after setup.

🎙 Say this to your botHi, your name is [Bob]. You're my assistant for [the Funding Hub]. I'm in the [Mountain] Time Zone. I like short, friendly messages with bullet points. Always draft emails for me to preview, never send anything without my okay.
  1. aGive it a name
  2. bGive it its job. It saves it
Step 4 · Composio

Why Composio?

Connect apps›Composio›Add
  1. Connect once. Composio links your bot to 1,000+ apps through their APIs.
  2. Future-proof. Move to a new tool later? Connect it to Composio and all your apps come with you.
I did exactly this. When I moved over from Claude, my apps came with me through Composio.

Step 7 · Get to know you · 3 of 3

Check what it learned

Check itTell me what you know about me so far.
  1. Read it. Anything wrong or missing?
  2. Correct it: "No, my bookkeeper handles invoices, not me."
  3. Then say "Remember this."
Step 8 · Make it better every day

Teach it your style

1 · Correct it

"Shorter. No 'hope this finds you well.' Sign off with just my first name."

2 · Say the magic words

"Remember this."

3 · Next time

It writes it your way, without being told.

Every correction you save makes tomorrow's drafts better.

How to talk to it

Text it like a sharp new hire

  • Be specific. "3 posts", not "some posts"
  • Give context. Who, what deal, what for
  • Draft first. You review before anything goes out
  • One thing at a time. Finish, then ask the next
  • Ask why. "Why did you pick these 5?"
Safety · 1 of 2

Stay in control

  • Draft first. I press send.
  • Never paste passwords, SSNs or bank logins into chat.
    Logins open the real sign-in page. Never type them in chat.
  • Read approval cards before you tap.
  • Double-check numbers. Every time.
Safety · 2 of 2

Random emails aren't your boss

Your bot shouldn't follow instructions found inside an email. Only yours.

Something feels off?

"Stop. Tell me your plan."

The golden rule
Your bot drafts, prepares, organizes.
You approve, send, sign, spend.
Homework · one a day until Call 2

6 prompts, one a day until Call 2

1Ask me questions, one at a time, so you can learn about me, my businesses, my goals and how I like to work. Save what you learn.
2Go through my inbox from the last 24 hours. Tell me the 5 that need me and draft replies. Don't send.
3Every weekday at 7 AM, send me a recap: today's calendar, emails that need me, anything due.
4Remind me [day] at [time] to [call/do what].
5Here's an email I wrote. Learn my style from it. Remember this.
6Every Friday at 4 PM, send me a weekly summary: what got done, what's open, what's next.
